insight.title: How the invisible dance shapes your morning
insight.subtitle: Beneath the surface of the stillest room, everything is in motion

sections.text: You are standing in a room that is never still. Even when the air feels silent and your coffee looks motionless, a frantic energy hums beneath. Every object holds a sea of vibrating particles, bumping together in an endless rush. We live inside a world that is constantly, quietly shivering.

This secret movement is what we call heat. When you hold a warm mug, you feel a literal transfer of motion. Fast-moving molecules in the clay strike the slower ones in your palms, sharing momentum like tiny billiard balls. It is an invisible negotiation between every object you touch.

This hidden system ensures that nothing remains isolated. Every breath you take and every step you make adjusts the temperature of the universe. We are not just observers, but participants in a grand balance. Your smallest gesture ripples outward, changing the rhythm of the molecules around you forever.
Warmth is the feeling of the universe sharing its energy with you.

news.title: Israel kills Islamic Guards intel chief, bombs largest Iranian petrochemical plant
news.description: Military also kills head of Quds Force's clandestine Unit 840; Katz vows that Israel will 'hunt down' Iran's leaders until the end; strikes hit airports used by IRGC
news.why: Rising conflict could soon disrupt global supply chains and fuel prices.

news.title: White House: ‘Trump has not yet signed off’ on 45‑day Iran ceasefire, war continues
news.description: The White House confirmed a 45-day ceasefire proposal with Iran is under consideration, but President Donald Trump has “not signed off on it,” with Operation Epic Fury continuing.
news.why: Ongoing instability makes international travel and shipping more expensive.

news.title: Wells Fargo no longer expects Fed rate cuts in 2026 as Iran war drags on
news.description: Wells ​Fargo Investment Institute said on Monday it ​no longer expects the U.S. Federal Reserve to cut interest rates in 2026, citing uncertainty around inflation and heightened geopolitical ‌risks tied ⁠to ⁠the Middle East war.
news.why: Your mortgage and loan repayments may remain expensive for years.

news.title: AI Job Cuts Could Lead to Years of Lower Pay for Displaced Workers: GS
news.description: Historically, workers displaced by new tech have made less and been more at risk for unemployment for years to come, Goldman Sachs said.
news.why: Automation could permanently lower your future salary and career stability.

news.title: Health care costs are Americans' top worry, Gallup says
news.description: A new Gallup poll reveals health care access and affordability is Americans' top concern, surpassing the economy and inflation.
news.why: Medical bills and insurance premiums may consume more of your budget.

news.title: Microsoft Signals AI Caution as Copilot Terms Highlight Reliability Limits
news.description: Microsoft has reinforced the limitations of AI systems through updated scrutiny of its Copilot terms of use, as the company continues expanding enterprise
news.why: You should double-check AI-generated work to avoid costly professional mistakes.

news.title: Samsung to shut down Samsung Messages in July, urging users to switch to Google Messages
news.description: Samsung is saying goodbye its namesake texting app. According to an end of service announcement published on the tech giant’s U.S. support website, Samsung Messages will be discontinued in July.
news.why: You will need to move your texts to a different app.
